thread.title_full: David L. Harrison appointed Poet Laureate for Route 66 Centennial Kickoff in Springfield

author: Y. B. Mcgovern
title: David L. Harrison appointed Poet Laureate for Route 66 Centennial Kickoff in Springfield
text:
David L. Harrison has been named Poet Laureate for the National Route 66 Centennial Kickoff Celebration by Mayor Jeff Schrag, according to a Mar. 18 announcement. The celebration will take place in Springfield from April 30 to May 3.
The appointment highlights the city’s role as the Birthplace of Route 66 and brings attention to its ongoing efforts in historic preservation, as reported by the official website of Springfield. Harrison, who has served as Poet Laureate for Drury University since 1983 and was Missouri’s Poet Laureate from 2023 to 2025, will present five original poems at various events during the centennial kickoff.
Scheduled events include dedications, a concert, a parade, and the Telegraph Ball. At each event, Harrison will read a poem written specifically for the occasion. For example, he will read “Where a Highway Was Born” at the Dedication of Birthplace Plaza on April 30 and “Showtime” via video before the kickoff concert that evening. Other poems include “Homecoming,” “Traveling the Memory,” and “66 is Catchier.”
Harrison reflected on his career path: “In a writing course that I took at Drury during my senior year, Professor Clark Graham liked my work and urged me to consider becoming a writer. I’m leaving out the years of struggle that followed before my first book was published 10 years later, a picture book that set my compass as a children’s writer. So far, I’ve published 23 books of poetry, 44 books of fiction, 24 books of nonfiction, and 19 books for classroom teachers.” His career has also included roles as pharmacologist, editorial manager for Hallmark Cards, and owner of Glenstone Block Company from 1973 to 2008.
Mayor Schrag said: “Route 66 carried messages across our nation: stories of hope, resilience and reinvention. David L. Harrison’s canon of work honors that legacy of communication and connection – how stories traveled long before social media, and how they still travel today. I am honored that David has agreed to serve as the Poet Laureate for this once-in-a-lifetime event for Springfield, Missouri – the National Route 66 Centennial Kickoff Celebration.”
Springfield operates under a council-manager form of government adopted in 1953 with a nine-member City Council responsible for setting policy and direction according to the official website. The city focuses on ethical local governance aimed at community benefits and cooperation according to its official website. It serves as county seat of Greene County in southwestern Missouri according to city records.
Springfield’s history includes being established in the 1830s when John Polk Campbell donated land in 1833; it incorporated as a town in 1838 according to historical accounts. The city was also site of significant events such as the Battle of Wilson’s Creek during the Civil War and played an important role in establishing Route 66 through its public square as noted by city sources.
Earlier this year Harrison donated more than fifty boxes of his work to Missouri State University’s Meyer Library where they are available within Special Collections.
